result.markdown: # Operators ![](/images/calculator.png){style="width:200px; border-radius:15px" fig-align="center"} __Operators__ are symbols in R that allow you to carry out many common tasks. The 3 main types of __operators__ in R are arithmetic, logical, and bitwise. We will ignore logical and bitwise and have a look at some arithmetic __operators__. The four most commonly used arithmetic __operators__ are: - `+` : Addition - `-` : Minus - `/` : Divide - `*` : Multiply ## Basic arithmetic Run the following commands in your RStudio __console__. ::: {.callout-note} Each line below represents one command. Once a command is typed out press enter to run the command. ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} 2+2 7-7 10/5 3*3 6+2+4 8-1-3 ``` ::: ## BODMAS R follows the BODMAS rules (Brackets, Orders (powers/roots), Division, Multiplication, Addition, Subtraction). Try out the following commands to demonstrate the usefulness of brackets. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} 3 + 2 * 2/5 ((3+2) * 2) / 5 3 - 2*4 + 1 (3-2) * (4+1) 3 * 3/2 * 2 - 1 (3*3) / ((2*2) - 1) ``` ::: When entering commands via the __console__ the results/output is printed to the screen (ignore the [1] at the moment). However, this is no better than a normal calculator currently. R is a lot more powerful as we shall see. ::: {.callout-note} The amount of space between the integers/numbers and an __operator__ does not matter in `R`. It is a matter of preference and clarity. ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: ::: {.cell-output-display} ```{=html} ``` ::: :::
